content: 1. Ethinylestradiol and Cyclophosphamide: Cyclophosphamide may increase the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. Close monitoring is advised. 2. Ethinylestradiol and Cyclosporine: Cyclosporine can increase the levels or effects of etonogestrel by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Ethinylestradiol may also increase cyclosporine levels through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Ethinylestradiol and Dabrafenib: Dabrafenib decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 4. Ethinylestradiol and Danazol: Danazol may increase the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. Close monitoring is advised. 5. Ethinylestradiol and Danicopan: Danicopan increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol through mechanisms involving BCRP substrates. Dose adjustments for BCRP substrates may be necessary. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Ethinylestradiol and Darifenacin: Darifenacin increases the levels or effects of etonogestrel by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Ethinylestradiol and Darunavir: Darunavir increases the levels of etonogestrel but decreases the levels of ethinylestradiol by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Non-hormonal contraceptives are recommended. 8. Ethinylestradiol and Dasatinib: Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of dasatinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dasatinib also increases the levels of etonogestrel. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Ethinylestradiol and Deferasirox: Deferasirox decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and etonogestrel by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Ethinylestradiol and Demeclocycline: Demeclocycline decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Ethinylestradiol and Desipramine: Ethinylestradiol may decrease the oxidative metabolism of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) like desipramine, potentially increasing serum concentrations and adverse effects. The interaction mechanism is unspecified. Monitor closely. 12. Ethinylestradiol and Dexamethasone: Dexamethasone decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Non-hormonal contraceptives are recommended. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Ethinylestradiol and DHEA (Herbal): DHEA increases the levels or effects of etonogestrel by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Ethinylestradiol and Diazepam: Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of diazepam by inhibiting its metabolism, leading to higher serum concentrations. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Ethinylestradiol and Dicloxacillin: Dicloxacillin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Ethinylestradiol and Doxepin: Ethinylestradiol may decrease the oxidative metabolism of TCAs like doxepin, potentially increasing serum concentrations and adverse effects. The interaction mechanism is unspecified. Monitor closely. 17. Ethinylestradiol and Doxycycline: Doxycycline decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Ethinylestradiol and Dronedarone: Dronedarone increases the levels or effects of etonogestrel by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Ethinylestradiol and Drospirenone: Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. Monitor closely. 20. Ethinylestradiol and Duloxetine: Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of duloxetine by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. Monitor closely. 21. Ethinylestradiol and Efavirenz: Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and etonogestrel by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Non-hormonal contraceptives are recommended. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Ethinylestradiol and Elafibranor: Elafibranor decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by weakly inducing CYP3A4. Switch to effective non-hormonal contraceptives or add a barrier method during and for at least three weeks after elafibranor treatment. Monitor closely. 23. Ethinylestradiol and Elagolix: Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by weakly to moderately inducing CYP3A4. Estrogen-containing contraceptives may reduce elagolix efficacy. Non-hormonal contraceptives are recommended during and for one week after elagolix treatment. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Ethinylestradiol and Eltrombopag: Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of eltrombopag by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Ethinylestradiol and Elvitegravir: Elvitegravir decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by an unknown mechanism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Non-hormonal contraceptives are recommended. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Ethinylestradiol and Enasidenib: Enasidenib increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol through mechanisms involving OATP1B1, OATP1B3, or BCRP substrates. Avoid coadministration with sensitive substrates. Monitor closely. 27. Ethinylestradiol and Encorafenib: Encorafenib decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Non-hormonal contraceptives are recommended. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 28. Ethinylestradiol and Enoxaparin: Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of enoxaparin by pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. This combination is contraindicated. 29. Ethinylestradiol and Enzalutamide: Enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Ethinylestradiol and Eplerenone: Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of eplerenone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. Monitor closely. 31. Ethinylestradiol and Erythromycin: Erythromycin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Ethinylestradiol and Felbamate: Felbamate decreases the levels of ethinylestradiol by an unknown mechanism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. Monitor closely. 33. Ethinylestradiol and Fexinidazole: Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 34. Ethinylestradiol and Fezolinetant: Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of fezolinetant by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 35. Ethinylestradiol and Finererone: Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of finererone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor serum potassium during initiation and dosage adjustments. Adjust finererone dosage as needed. Monitor closely. 36. Ethinylestradiol and Flibanserin: Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
